The isolated artifact's question about the necessity of engine separation is only well-posed because authoring a claim conditionally biases the same engine's probability mass toward its own output (SRC_002's mechanism). If this bias mechanism did not hold for a given engine architecture (e.g., a frozen verification module), the separation question would be vacuous. It is refuted if a single engine can provably avoid the conditional bias described in SRC_002, in which case the problem's premise that separation is even at issue is false.
